# Rivermax Utils

[![GitHub license](https://img.shields.io/github/license/NVIDIA/nvidia-docker?style=flat-square)](https://github.com/nvidia/rivermax-utils/blob/main/License.md)

This repository contains utility scripts and tools for NVIDIA Rivermax SDK, providing essential tools for system optimization, performance tuning, and various utilities across different platforms.

## Overview

NVIDIA Rivermax Utils provides a comprehensive set of tools designed to enhance the Rivermax experience by offering system tuning capabilities, performance optimization scripts, and other utility functions to improve your Rivermax development and deployment workflow.

## Repository Structure

### Linux Tools
- **[`rmx_perf/linux/`](./rmx_perf/linux/)** - Advanced performance tool
  - Discover NVIDIA network devices
  - Tune system, network, CPU, GRUB
  - Query current system state
  - Monitor PTP/PHC synchronization
  - Manage PTP services
- **[`media_converter/`](./media_converter/)** - MP4 to SMPTE ST 2110-20 raw media format converter

### Windows Tools
- **[`windows_tuning/`](./windows_tuning/)** - Tuning scripts
  - System optimization and network interface tuning
  - Available functionality: check, set and restore system tuning

## Getting Started

Clone the repository:
```sh
git clone https://github.com/nvidia/rivermax-utils.git
```

Navigate to the specific tool directory for detailed usage instructions.

## Issues and Contribution

We welcome contributions to the Rivermax Utils repository:  
* To contribute and make pull requests, please follow the guidelines outlined in the [Contributing](CONTRIBUTING.md) document.
* Please let us know about any bugs or issues by [filing a new issue](https://github.com/NVIDIA/rivermax-utils/issues/new).

## License

This project is licensed under the same terms as the Rivermax SDK. See the [License](License.md) file for details.

# Rivermax Windows Tuning Scripts

## Description

This directory contains two scripts designed to automate and optimize the tuning of system and network interface settings for systems using the Rivermax library. 
These scripts help enhance performance by adjusting various system and interface parameters.

## system_tuning Script

The System Tuning script automates the optimization of general system settings. 

#### Key features

- Changing the current power plan to High performance.
- Increasing the paging file size to a maximum of 15360 MB.
- Disabling system visual effects (if possible).
- Disabling search indexing.
- Enabling Large Pages Support.
- Disabling the w32time service.

The script allows you to check system compliance, save initial settings to a JSON file and tune requirements, or restore initial settings.

To see all available options, run:

```powershell
system_tuning.ps1 -h
```

#### Prerequisites

- Windows Server 2019, Windows Server 2022, Windows 10 PRO, Windows 11 PRO, or Windows 20HS.
- Administrative privileges.

#### Example

```powershell
system_tuning.ps1 -c
system_tuning.ps1 -s -f "C:\Users\<some username>\systemOriginalSettings.json"
system_tuning.ps1 -r -f "C:\Users\<some username>\systemOriginalSettings.json"
```

#### Limitations

For achieving better performance, consider disabling Windows Defender, disabling unnecessary tasks and applications, and tuning the BIOS.
Find the Rivermax Performance Tuning Guide on the [NVIDIA Rivermax Getting Started page](https://developer.nvidia.com/networking/rivermax-getting-started)

## interface_tuning Script

The Interface Tuning script automates the tuning of network adapter settings.

#### Key features

- Tuning NUMA Selection.
- Disabling Flow Control.
- Disabling Local Port Loopback.

The script allows you to check adapter compliance, save initial settings to a JSON file and tune requirements, or restore initial settings. 
You need to specify an adapter name and can also specify the profile {Both | Send | Receive; default=Both}.

To see all available options, run:

```powershell
interface_tuning.ps1 -h
```

#### Prerequisites

- Windows Server 2019, Windows Server 2022, Windows 10 PRO, Windows 11 PRO, or Windows 20HS.
- Administrative privileges.
- Adapter name to be tuned.

#### Profiles

- **'Both'** or **'Send'**: The script will check, set, and reset the selection of the closest NUMA to the NIC, disabling flow control and local Loopback if present.
- **'Receive'**: The script will only check, set, and reset the flow control of the valid NIC given.

#### Example

```powershell
interface_tuning.ps1 -c -i "Ethernet 2"
interface_tuning.ps1 -s -i "Ethernet 2" -p "Both" -f "C:\Users\<some username>\InterfaceOriginalSettings.json"
interface_tuning.ps1 -r -i "Ethernet 2" -p "Send" -f "C:\Users\<some username>\InterfaceOriginalSettings.json"
```

# Media File Generator

Convert MP4 video files to raw media formats compatible with **SMPTE ST 2110-20** Professional Media Over Managed IP Networks: Uncompressed Active Video.

## Overview

This tool converts standard MP4 video files into raw packed formats suitable for use with NVIDIA Rivermax SDK and SMPTE ST 2110 video streaming workflows.

> ⚠️ **Note:** This tool is in early development and has not been thoroughly tested across all format combinations.

### Supported Output Formats

| Format | Description | Bit Depths | Resolutions |
|--------|-------------|------------|-------------|
| `ycbcr422` | YCbCr 4:2:2 chroma subsampling | 10-bit, 12-bit | FHD, UHD |
| `ycbcr420` | YCbCr 4:2:0 chroma subsampling | 10-bit only | FHD, UHD |
| `rgb` | RGB color space | 8-bit, 10-bit, 12-bit | FHD, UHD |

### Valid Combinations

| Format | FHD/8 | FHD/10 | FHD/12 | UHD/8 | UHD/10 | UHD/12 |
|--------|:-----:|:------:|:------:|:-----:|:------:|:------:|
| ycbcr422 | ✗ | ${\color{green}✓}$ | ${\color{green}✓}$ | ✗ | ${\color{green}✓}$ | ${\color{green}✓}$ |
| ycbcr420 | ✗ | ${\color{green}✓}$ | ✗ | ✗ | ${\color{green}✓}$ | ✗ |
| rgb | ${\color{green}✓}$ | ${\color{green}✓}$ | ${\color{green}✓}$ | ${\color{green}✓}$ | ${\color{green}✓}$ | ${\color{green}✓}$ |

## Quick Start

**Prerequisites:** Make sure ffmpeg and build tools (make, g++) are installed (see Installation section below).

```bash
# Build the converter first (one-time setup)
./generate_media_file.sh --build

# Basic YCbCr 4:2:2 conversion
./generate_media_file.sh -i input.mp4 -o output.ycbcr -f ycbcr422

# RGB 8-bit (fast - no converter needed)
./generate_media_file.sh -i input.mp4 -o output.rgb -f rgb -b 8

# UHD 12-bit with custom duration
./generate_media_file.sh -i input.mp4 -o output.ycbcr -f ycbcr422 -r UHD -b 12 -d 10
```

## Installation

### Prerequisites

You need to install these dependencies manually:

- **ffmpeg** - Video processing tool for decoding MP4 files and converting them to raw formats
- **make, g++** - Build tools required to compile the media_converter

### Installing Dependencies

**Debian/Ubuntu:**
```bash
sudo apt-get update
sudo apt-get install ffmpeg build-essential
```

**RHEL/CentOS/Fedora:**
```bash
# RHEL/CentOS
sudo yum install epel-release
sudo yum install ffmpeg
sudo yum groupinstall "Development Tools"

# Fedora
sudo dnf install ffmpeg
sudo dnf groupinstall "Development Tools"
```

### Building media_converter

After installing the dependencies, build the media_converter binary:

```bash
# Option 1: Use the built-in build command
./generate_media_file.sh --build

# Option 2: Build manually
cd src && make media_converter
```

The `--build` flag checks build dependencies (make, g++) and builds media_converter if it's missing.

## Usage

```
./generate_media_file.sh -i <MP4_FILE> -o <OUTPUT_FILE> -f <FORMAT> [OPTIONS]
```

### Required Parameters

| Flag | Parameter | Description |
|------|-----------|-------------|
| `-i` | `<MP4_FILE>` | Input MP4 file to convert |
| `-o` | `<OUTPUT_FILE>` | Output file name (e.g., output.ycbcr) |
| `-f` | `<FORMAT>` | Pixel format: `ycbcr422`, `ycbcr420`, or `rgb` |

### Optional Parameters

| Flag | Parameter | Default | Description |
|------|-----------|---------|-------------|
| `-r` | `<RESOLUTION>` | FHD | Resolution: `FHD` (1920×1080) or `UHD` (3840×2160) |
| `-b` | `<BIT_DEPTH>` | 10 | Bit depth: `8`, `10`, or `12` (8 only for rgb) |
| `-p` | `<FPS>` | 50 | Frame rate in frames per second |
| `-d` | `<DURATION>` | 3 | Duration in seconds to extract |
| `-s` | `<START_TIME>` | 0 | Start time offset in seconds |

### Help

```bash
# Quick help
./generate_media_file.sh -h

# Full documentation
./generate_media_file.sh --help
```

## Examples

#### YCbCr 4:2:2 10-bit FHD

```bash
./generate_media_file.sh -i video.mp4 -o video.ycbcr -f ycbcr422 -r FHD -b 10
```

#### YCbCr 4:2:0 10-bit UHD (starting at 30 seconds)

```bash
./generate_media_file.sh -i video.mp4 -o video.ycbcr -f ycbcr420 -r UHD -s 30
```

#### RGB 12-bit at 60fps

```bash
./generate_media_file.sh -i video.mp4 -o video.rgb -f rgb -b 12 -p 60
```

#### RGB 8-bit (fast conversion)

```bash
./generate_media_file.sh -i video.mp4 -o video.rgb -f rgb -b 8
```

> **Note:** RGB 8-bit uses direct ffmpeg output and skips the converter step.

#### Extract 5 seconds starting at 1 minute

```bash
./generate_media_file.sh -i video.mp4 -o clip.ycbcr -f ycbcr422 -d 5 -s 60
```

## Conversion Process

### Format Transformation

**ffmpeg** outputs video in planar format, where each color component (Y, Cb, Cr or R, G, B) is stored in a separate continuous plane:

```
Planar:  YYYY... CbCbCb... CrCrCr...  (separate planes)
```

**SMPTE ST 2110-20** requires packed format, where color components are interleaved per pixel group:

```
Packed:  Cb Y Cr Y Cb Y Cr Y...       (interleaved samples)
```

The **media_converter** performs this planar-to-packed conversion and handles bit-packing.

### For YCbCr and RGB 10/12-bit

1. **ffmpeg** extracts raw video from MP4 in planar format
2. **media_converter** transforms planar to packed format
3. Output file is ready for SMPTE ST 2110-20 streaming

### For RGB 8-bit

1. **ffmpeg** converts MP4 directly to RGB24 packed format
2. No additional conversion needed (faster)

## File Structure

```
├── generate_media_file.sh   # Main conversion script
├── README.md                # This file
└── src/                     # Backend implementation
    ├── media_converter.cpp  # C++ converter source
    └── Makefile             # Build configuration
```

## Supported Platforms

- **Linux only** (This tool was developed on Ubuntu)
- Requires bash installed on the system

# Rivermax Linux Performance Tool

## Overview

The `rmx_perf` tool is a comprehensive bash-based performance tuning and monitoring utility for Linux systems running NVIDIA Rivermax SDK applications. It automates the recommendations from the NVIDIA Rivermax Performance Tuning Guide.

## Documentation

**[View Full Documentation](https://nvidia.github.io/rivermax-utils/rmx_perf/)**

The GitHub Pages documentation includes:
- Detailed command reference for all options and modes
- Usage examples for Device, Tune, Query, Monitor, and PTP operations
- Testing guide
- Getting started workflow

## Main Components

The tool provides several operation modes:

- **Devices (`-d`)** - Discover NVIDIA network devices with detailed information
- **Tune (`-t`)** - Apply performance tuning (network, CPU, OS, GRUB)
- **Query (`-q`)** - Report current system state without making changes
- **Monitor (`-m`)** - Continuous PTP/PHC synchronization monitoring
- **Run PTP (`--rp`)** - Configure and start PTP services (ptp4l, phc2sys)
- **Stop PTP (`--sp`)** - Stop PTP services
- **Install Tools (`--it`)** - Install required system packages

## Basic Commands

```bash
# Show available NVIDIA network devices
sudo ./rmx_perf -d

# Tune system with default settings
sudo ./rmx_perf -i eth0 -t

# Query current settings (no changes)
sudo ./rmx_perf -i eth0 -q

# Monitor PTP/PHC synchronization
sudo ./rmx_perf -i eth0 -m
```

## Resources

- **Documentation**: [View online documentation](https://nvidia.github.io/rivermax-utils/rmx_perf/)
- **Built-in Help**: `./rmx_perf --help`
- **NVIDIA Rivermax Performance Tuning Guide**: Find it on the [NVIDIA Rivermax Getting Started page](https://developer.nvidia.com/networking/rivermax-getting-started)
- **Report Issues**: [File a new issue](https://github.com/NVIDIA/rivermax-utils/issues/new) on GitHub

CC=g++
CFLAGS=-std=c++14 -g -O2
APPS=media_converter
LFLAGS=

media_converter_OBJS=media_converter.o

all: $(APPS)

%.o: %.cpp
	$(CC) -o $@ $(CFLAGS) -c $<

media_converter: $(media_converter_OBJS)
	$(CC) -o $@ $(LFLAGS) $^

clean:
	@echo cleaning apps
	@rm -f $(APPS)

cleanall: clean
	@echo cleaning obj files
	@rm -f *.o

# Security

NVIDIA is dedicated to the security and trust of our software products and services, including all source code repositories managed through our organization.

If you need to report a security issue, please use the appropriate contact points outlined below. **Please do not report security vulnerabilities through GitHub/GitLab.**

To report a potential security vulnerability in any NVIDIA product:

- Web: [Security Vulnerability Submission Form](https://www.nvidia.com/object/submit-security-vulnerability.html)
- E-Mail: [psirt@nvidia.com](mailto:psirt@nvidia.com)

  - Please include the following information:
    - Product/Driver name and version/branch that contains the vulnerability
    - Type of vulnerability (code execution, denial of service, buffer overflow, etc.)

    - Proof-of-concept or exploit code
    - Potential impact of the vulnerability, including how an attacker could exploit the vulnerability

While NVIDIA currently does not have a bug bounty program, we do offer acknowledgement when an externally reported security issue is addressed under our coordinated vulnerability disclosure policy. Please visit our [Product Security Incident Response Team (PSIRT)](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/security/psirt-policies/) policies page for more information.

## NVIDIA Product Security

For all security-related concerns, please visit NVIDIA's Product Security portal at [https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/security](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/security)

set -e

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"

# Function to get video duration in seconds
get_video_duration() {
    local input_file="$1"
    duration=$(ffprobe -v error -show_entries format=duration -of default=noprint_wrappers=1:nokey=1 "$input_file")
    echo "$duration"
}

# Script version
VERSION="1.0.0"

# Color codes (using $'...' for proper escape interpretation)
BOLD=$'\033[1m'
DIM=$'\033[2m'
C=$'\033[36m'    # Cyan for parameters/values
G=$'\033[32m'    # Green for formats/valid options
Y=$'\033[33m'    # Yellow for section headers
W=$'\033[97m'    # White/bright for emphasis
R=$'\033[0m'     # Reset

# Function to display brief usage (like rmx_perf -h)
usage() {
    cat << EOF
${Y}NAME${R}
    $(basename "$0") - convert MP4 files to SMPTE ST 2110-20 uncompressed raw media formats

${Y}SYNOPSIS${R}
    $(basename "$0") ${C}-i${R} FILE ${C}-o${R} FILE ${C}-f${R} FORMAT [${C}-r${R} RES] [${C}-b${R} DEPTH] [<OPTIONS>]
    $(basename "$0") ${C}-h${R} | ${C}--help${R}

${Y}DESCRIPTION${R}
    Media File Generator ${VERSION} for NVIDIA Rivermax

    Convert MP4 video files to raw packed formats for SMPTE ST 2110-20 streaming.

    ffmpeg outputs ${W}planar${R} formats (color planes stored separately), but
    SMPTE ST 2110-20 requires ${W}packed${R} formats (pixels interleaved).
    The media_converter performs this planar-to-packed conversion.

    For RGB 8-bit, ffmpeg outputs packed rgb24 directly (no converter needed).

    Use ${C}--help${R} for detailed format information.

${Y}OPTIONS${R}

  ${W}Required Options${R}
    ${C}-i${R}, ${C}--input${R} <FILE>         Input MP4 file to convert
    ${C}-o${R}, ${C}--output${R} <FILE>        Output file name (e.g., output.ycbcr)
    ${C}-f${R}, ${C}--format${R} <FORMAT>      Pixel format: ${G}ycbcr422${R}, ${G}ycbcr420${R}, ${G}rgb${R}

  ${W}Video Options${R}
    ${C}-r${R}, ${C}--resolution${R} <RES>     Resolution: ${G}FHD${R}, ${G}UHD${R} [default: ${G}FHD${R}]
    ${C}-b${R}, ${C}--bit-depth${R} <DEPTH>    Bit depth: ${G}8${R}, ${G}10${R}, ${G}12${R} (8 only for rgb) [default: ${G}10${R}]
    ${C}-p${R}, ${C}--frame-rate${R} <FPS>     Frame rate in frames per second [default: ${G}50${R}]

  ${W}Extraction Options${R}
    ${C}-d${R}, ${C}--duration${R} <SECS>      Duration in seconds to extract [default: ${G}3${R}]
    ${C}-s${R}, ${C}--start${R} <SECS>         Start time offset in seconds [default: ${G}0${R}]

  ${W}General Options${R}
    ${C}-h${R}                         Show brief help and exit
    ${C}--help${R}                     Show full help with format details and exit
    ${C}--build${R}                    Check build dependencies (make, g++) and build media_converter if missing

${Y}EXAMPLES${R}
    ${DIM}\$${R} $(basename "$0") -i video.mp4 -o out.ycbcr -f ycbcr422
    ${DIM}\$${R} $(basename "$0") -i video.mp4 -o out.rgb -f rgb -b 8 -d 5
    ${DIM}\$${R} $(basename "$0") -i video.mp4 -o out.ycbcr -f ycbcr420 -r UHD -s 30

Run '$(basename "$0") ${C}--help${R}' for full documentation including format details.
EOF
    exit 1
}

# Function to display full/detailed usage (like rmx_perf --help)
full_usage() {
    cat << EOF
${Y}NAME${R}
    $(basename "$0") - convert MP4 files to SMPTE ST 2110-20 uncompressed raw media formats

${Y}SYNOPSIS${R}

    $(basename "$0") ${C}-i${R} FILE ${C}-o${R} FILE ${C}-f${R} FORMAT [${C}-r${R} RES] [${C}-b${R} DEPTH] [<OPTIONS>]
    $(basename "$0") ${C}-h${R} | ${C}--help${R}

${Y}DESCRIPTION${R}

    Media File Generator ${VERSION} for NVIDIA Rivermax

    Convert MP4 video files to raw packed formats suitable for use with
    NVIDIA Rivermax SDK and SMPTE ST 2110-20 uncompressed video streaming workflows.

    ${W}Why is conversion needed?${R}

    ffmpeg outputs video in ${W}planar${R} format, where each color component
    (Y, Cb, Cr or R, G, B) is stored in a separate continuous plane:

        Planar:  YYYY... CbCbCb... CrCrCr...  (separate planes)

    SMPTE ST 2110-20 uncompressed raw media formats requires ${W}packed${R} format,
    where color components are interleaved per pixel group:

        Packed:  Cb Y Cr Y Cb Y Cr Y...       (interleaved samples)

    The ${C}media_converter${R} performs this planar-to-packed conversion
    and handles the bit-packing for 10-bit and 12-bit depths.

    ${W}Exception:${R} For RGB 8-bit, ffmpeg outputs packed rgb24 directly,
    so no converter is needed.

${Y}OPTIONS${R}

  ${W}Required Options${R}
    ${C}-i${R}, ${C}--input${R} <FILE>         Input MP4 file to convert

    ${C}-o${R}, ${C}--output${R} <FILE>        Output file name (e.g., output.ycbcr, output.rgb)

    ${C}-f${R}, ${C}--format${R} <FORMAT>      Pixel format (see FORMATS section below)

  ${W}Video Options${R}
    ${C}-r${R}, ${C}--resolution${R} <RES>     Video resolution [default: ${G}FHD${R}]
                               ${G}FHD${R} = 1920x1080
                               ${G}UHD${R} = 3840x2160

    ${C}-b${R}, ${C}--bit-depth${R} <DEPTH>    Color bit depth [default: ${G}10${R}]
                               ${G}8${R}  = 8-bit  (rgb only)
                               ${G}10${R} = 10-bit
                               ${G}12${R} = 12-bit

    ${C}-p${R}, ${C}--frame-rate${R} <FPS>     Output frame rate in fps [default: ${G}50${R}]

  ${W}Extraction Options${R}
    ${C}-d${R}, ${C}--duration${R} <SECS>      Duration in seconds to extract [default: ${G}3${R}]

    ${C}-s${R}, ${C}--start${R} <SECS>         Start time offset in seconds [default: ${G}0${R}]

  ${W}General Options${R}
    ${C}-h${R}                         Show brief help and exit

    ${C}--help${R}                     Show full help and exit

    ${C}--build${R}                    Check build dependencies (make, g++) and build media_converter if missing

${Y}FORMATS${R}

  ${G}ycbcr422${R} (YCbCr 4:2:2)
    Bit depths:   ${G}10${R}, ${G}12${R}
    Resolutions:  ${G}FHD${R}, ${G}UHD${R}
    ffmpeg fmt:   yuv422p10le, yuv422p12le

  ${G}ycbcr420${R} (YCbCr 4:2:0)
    Bit depths:   ${G}10${R} only (12-bit NOT supported)
    Resolutions:  ${G}FHD${R}, ${G}UHD${R}
    ffmpeg fmt:   yuv420p10le

  ${G}rgb${R} (RGB)
    Bit depths:   ${G}8${R}, ${G}10${R}, ${G}12${R}
    Resolutions:  ${G}FHD${R}, ${G}UHD${R}
    ffmpeg fmt:   rgb24, gbrp10le, gbrp12le
    Note:         8-bit skips converter (direct ffmpeg output)

${Y}VALID COMBINATIONS${R}

    Format      FHD/8   FHD/10  FHD/12  UHD/8   UHD/10  UHD/12
    ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    ycbcr422      ✗       ${G}✓${R}       ${G}✓${R}       ✗       ${G}✓${R}       ${G}✓${R}
    ycbcr420      ✗       ${G}✓${R}       ✗       ✗       ${G}✓${R}       ✗
    rgb           ${G}✓${R}       ${G}✓${R}       ${G}✓${R}       ${G}✓${R}       ${G}✓${R}       ${G}✓${R}

${Y}EXAMPLES${R}

    ${DIM}# Basic YCbCr 4:2:2 10-bit FHD conversion${R}
        ${DIM}\$${R} ./generate_media_file.sh -i input.mp4 -o output.ycbcr -f ycbcr422

    ${DIM}# YCbCr 4:2:2 12-bit UHD, first 10 seconds${R}
        ${DIM}\$${R} ./generate_media_file.sh -i input.mp4 -o output.ycbcr -f ycbcr422 -r UHD -b 12 -d 10

    ${DIM}# YCbCr 4:2:0 10-bit, starting at 30 seconds${R}
        ${DIM}\$${R} $(basename "$0") -i input.mp4 -o output.ycbcr -f ycbcr420 -s 30

    ${DIM}# RGB 8-bit FHD (fast, no converter needed)${R}
        ${DIM}\$${R} $(basename "$0") -i input.mp4 -o output.rgb -f rgb -b 8

    ${DIM}# RGB 12-bit at 60fps${R}
        ${DIM}\$${R} $(basename "$0") -i input.mp4 -o output.rgb -f rgb -b 12 -p 60

${Y}DEPENDENCIES${R}

    ${C}ffmpeg${R}                     Video processing (required; install via your package manager)
    ${C}make${R}, ${C}g++${R}                  Build tools (required to build converter; install via your package manager)
    ${C}media_converter${R}   Format conversion (build: ${C}make -C src media_converter${R}; or ${C}--build${R})

${Y}SEE ALSO${R}

    NVIDIA Rivermax SDK Documentation
    SMPTE ST 2110-20: Professional Media Over Managed IP Networks: Uncompressed Active Video Specification
EOF
    exit 0
}

# Show usage if no arguments
if [ $# -eq 0 ]; then
    usage
fi

# Check for -h or --help
if [ "$1" = "-h" ]; then
    usage
fi

if [ "$1" = "--help" ]; then
    full_usage
fi

# Build media_converter (requires make and g++ already on the system).
build_converter() {
    echo "Building media_converter..."
    if [ -f "$SCRIPT_DIR/src/Makefile" ]; then
        (cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/src" && make media_converter)
        if [ $? -ne 0 ]; then
            echo "Error: Failed to build media_converter."
            return 1
        fi
    else
        echo "Error: Makefile not found in src/ directory."
        return 1
    fi
}

# Check build tools (make, g++) are present. Exits if not found.
check_build_tools() {
    if command -v make &> /dev/null && command -v g++ &> /dev/null; then
        echo "[✓] build tools (make, g++): present"
    else
        echo "[✗] build tools (make, g++): not found"
        echo "    Install manually: e.g. build-essential (Debian/Ubuntu), or Development Tools (RHEL/Fedora)"
        exit 1
    fi
}

# Handle --build: check build tools and build media_converter if missing
if [ "$1" = "--build" ]; then
    if [ $# -ne 1 ]; then
        echo "Error: --build takes no other arguments"
        echo "Usage: $(basename "$0") --build"
        exit 1
    fi
    echo "=== Checking build dependencies ==="
    echo ""
    check_build_tools
    if [ -f "$SCRIPT_DIR/src/media_converter" ]; then
        echo "[✓] media_converter: already built"
    else
        echo "[✗] media_converter: not built"
        echo "    Building..."
        if build_converter; then
            echo "[✓] media_converter: built successfully"
        else
            echo "    Build failed. Try manually: make -C src media_converter"
            exit 1
        fi
    fi
    echo ""
    echo "=== Build successful ==="
    exit 0
fi

for arg in "$@"; do
    if [ "$arg" = "--build" ]; then
        echo "Error: --build cannot be combined with conversion options"
        echo "Usage: $(basename "$0") --build"
        exit 1
    fi
done

# Before conversion: check required dependencies.
check_ffmpeg() {
    if ! command -v ffmpeg &> /dev/null; then
        echo "Error: ffmpeg is not installed (required for conversion)."
        echo "  Install manually: e.g. apt-get install ffmpeg, or yum install ffmpeg"
        echo "  Then run conversion again."
        exit 1
    fi
}

check_converter() {
    if [ ! -f "$SCRIPT_DIR/src/media_converter" ]; then
        echo "Error: media_converter is not built (required for this format)."
        echo "  Build manually: make -C src media_converter (requires make and g++)"
        echo "  Or run: $(basename "$0") --build"
        echo "  Then run conversion again."
        exit 1
    fi
}

# Initialize variables
INPUT_FILE=""
OUTPUT_FILE=""
FORMAT=""
RESOLUTION="FHD"
BIT_DEPTH="10"
TEMP_DIR="/tmp/media_conversion"
DURATION=3
START_TIME=0
FRAME_RATE=50

# Parse command line arguments (supports both short and long options)
while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
    case $1 in
        -i|--input)
            INPUT_FILE="$2"
            shift 2
            ;;
        -o|--output)
            OUTPUT_FILE="$2"
            shift 2
            ;;
        -f|--format)
            FORMAT="$2"
            shift 2
            ;;
        -r|--resolution)
            RESOLUTION="$2"
            shift 2
            ;;
        -b|--bit-depth)
            BIT_DEPTH="$2"
            shift 2
            ;;
        -d|--duration)
            DURATION="$2"
            shift 2
            ;;
        -s|--start)
            START_TIME="$2"
            shift 2
            ;;
        -p|--frame-rate)
            FRAME_RATE="$2"
            shift 2
            ;;
        -h)
            usage
            ;;
        *)
            echo "Error: Unknown option: $1"
            usage
            ;;
    esac
done

# Validate required parameters
if [ -z "$INPUT_FILE" ] || [ -z "$OUTPUT_FILE" ] || [ -z "$FORMAT" ]; then
    echo "Error: Missing required parameters"
    usage
fi

# Check required dependencies before conversion (ffmpeg required; media_converter for non-RGB-8-bit)
echo "Checking required dependencies..."
check_ffmpeg
# rgb 8-bit format doesn't need the converter - only ffmpeg
if [ "$FORMAT" != "rgb" ] || [ "$BIT_DEPTH" != "8" ]; then
    check_converter
fi

# Check if input file exists
if [ ! -f "$INPUT_FILE" ]; then
    echo "Error: Input file '$INPUT_FILE' does not exist"
    exit 1
fi

# Get video duration
VIDEO_DURATION=$(get_video_duration "$INPUT_FILE")
if [ -z "$VIDEO_DURATION" ]; then
    echo "Error: Could not get video duration"
    exit 1
fi

# Validate start time and duration
if (( $(echo "$START_TIME >= $VIDEO_DURATION" | bc -l) )); then
    echo "Error: Start time ($START_TIME) is beyond video duration ($VIDEO_DURATION)"
    exit 1
fi

if (( $(echo "$START_TIME + $DURATION > $VIDEO_DURATION" | bc -l) )); then
    echo "Warning: Requested duration exceeds available video length"
    echo "Adjusting duration from $DURATION to $(echo "$VIDEO_DURATION - $START_TIME" | bc -l) seconds"
    DURATION=$(echo "$VIDEO_DURATION - $START_TIME" | bc -l)
fi

# Validate format
case $FORMAT in
    ycbcr422|ycbcr420|rgb) ;;
    *) echo "Error: Invalid format. Must be ycbcr422, ycbcr420, or rgb"; usage;;
esac

# Validate resolution
case $RESOLUTION in
    FHD) RESOLUTION_STR="1920x1080";;
    UHD) RESOLUTION_STR="3840x2160";;
    *) echo "Error: Invalid resolution. Must be FHD or UHD"; usage;;
esac

# Validate bit depth (rgb supports 8-bit, others only 10/12)
if [ "$FORMAT" = "rgb" ]; then
    case $BIT_DEPTH in
        8|10|12) ;;
        *) echo "Error: Invalid bit depth for rgb. Must be 8, 10, or 12"; usage;;
    esac
else
    case $BIT_DEPTH in
        10|12) ;;
        *) echo "Error: Invalid bit depth. Must be 10 or 12"; usage;;
    esac
fi

# Validate YUV420 12-bit combination
if [ "$FORMAT" = "ycbcr420" ] && [ "$BIT_DEPTH" = "12" ]; then
    echo "Error: YUV420 format only supports 10-bit depth"
    usage
fi

# Create temporary directory
mkdir -p "$TEMP_DIR"
if [ "$FORMAT" = "rgb" ] && [ "$BIT_DEPTH" = "8" ]; then
    # rgb 8-bit outputs directly to final file (no converter needed)
    TEMP_FILE="$OUTPUT_FILE"
else
    TEMP_FILE="$TEMP_DIR/temp_$(basename "$OUTPUT_FILE")"
fi

# Set ffmpeg pixel format based on format and bit depth
case $FORMAT in
    ycbcr422)
        if [ "$BIT_DEPTH" = "10" ]; then
            PIX_FMT="yuv422p10le"
        else
            PIX_FMT="yuv422p12le"
        fi
        ;;
    ycbcr420)
        PIX_FMT="yuv420p10le"
        ;;
    rgb)
        if [ "$BIT_DEPTH" = "8" ]; then
            PIX_FMT="rgb24"
        elif [ "$BIT_DEPTH" = "10" ]; then
            PIX_FMT="gbrp10le"
        else
            PIX_FMT="gbrp12le"
        fi
        ;;
esac

echo "=== Starting Media Conversion ==="
echo "Input: $INPUT_FILE"
echo "Output: $OUTPUT_FILE"
echo "Format: $FORMAT"
echo "Resolution: $RESOLUTION ($RESOLUTION_STR)"
echo "Bit Depth: $BIT_DEPTH"
echo "Start Time: $START_TIME seconds"
echo "Duration: $DURATION seconds"
echo "Total Video Length: $VIDEO_DURATION seconds"
echo ""

# Step 1: Convert MP4 to raw format using ffmpeg
if [ "$FORMAT" = "rgb" ] && [ "$BIT_DEPTH" = "8" ]; then
    echo "Converting MP4 to RGB 8-bit packed format (direct output)..."
else
    echo "Step 1: Converting MP4 to raw format..."
fi
ffmpeg -y -ss "$START_TIME" -t "$DURATION" -i "$INPUT_FILE" -f rawvideo -vcodec rawvideo -pix_fmt "$PIX_FMT" -s "$RESOLUTION_STR" -r "$FRAME_RATE" "$TEMP_FILE"
if [ $? -ne 0 ]; then
    echo "Error: ffmpeg conversion failed"
    if [ "$FORMAT" != "rgb" ] || [ "$BIT_DEPTH" != "8" ]; then
        rm -f "$TEMP_FILE"
    fi
    exit 1
fi

# Step 2: Convert raw format to final format using media_converter (skip for rgb 8-bit)
if [ "$FORMAT" != "rgb" ] || [ "$BIT_DEPTH" != "8" ]; then
    echo "Step 2: Converting to final format..."
    case $FORMAT in
        ycbcr422)
            "$SCRIPT_DIR/src/media_converter" -i "$TEMP_FILE" -o "$OUTPUT_FILE" --vbd "$BIT_DEPTH" --vr "$RESOLUTION" --vst YUV422
            ;;
        ycbcr420)
            "$SCRIPT_DIR/src/media_converter" -i "$TEMP_FILE" -o "$OUTPUT_FILE" --vbd "$BIT_DEPTH" --vr "$RESOLUTION" --vst YUV420
            ;;
        rgb)
            "$SCRIPT_DIR/src/media_converter" -i "$TEMP_FILE" -o "$OUTPUT_FILE" --vbd "$BIT_DEPTH" --vr "$RESOLUTION" --vst GBR
            ;;
    esac

    if [ $? -ne 0 ]; then
        echo "Error: media_converter conversion failed"
        rm -f "$TEMP_FILE"
        exit 1
    fi

    # Cleanup temp file
    rm -f "$TEMP_FILE"
fi
echo "=== Generated $OUTPUT_FILE Successfully ==="
